title: Calculation Atelier
concept: An engineering calculation is composed like a carefully annotated drafting sheet. Four unit-bearing paper strips establish dimensional provenance; a hatched quadratic area becomes an algebraic balance; a quiet vermilion pump curve meets the chosen system curve; an explicitly assumed resistance interval becomes a visible uncertainty envelope; and a final review sheet preserves the solved candidate alongside unresolved OEM evidence and human selection. Oversized mathematical typography, warm paper, measured rules and finite ink-and-paper motion make the work legible without dashboard chrome. Every numerical relationship is illustrative and normalized, not performed plant engineering.
metaphor: An engineer's calculation atelier: dimensional specimens, geometric proof, and an unfinished review folio.
choreography: Four unit-bearing paper strips settle at staggered heights and connect to a shared provenance datum.
A quadratic hatched area and static-head strip establish the system; an equality and radical expose the flow solution.
The pump and chosen system curves draw, then their analytical intersection appears with its solved relative flow.
A resistance envelope washes around the system curve and projects the resulting flow interval onto the axis.
A review folio assembles with the selected numerical candidate, traced units and two visibly open review obligations.
interaction: The supplied base/alternate choice selects K=0.70 or K=1.50. The unchanged pump H=1−0.45Q² intersects H=0.12+KQ² at Q=sqrt(0.88/(K+0.45)): 0.874767 or 0.671775. Higher resistance therefore shifts the plotted point left and reduces relative flow by 23.2 percent. A ghost base intersection and leftward arrow make that change visible. Review and outcome retain the selected state.
contributions: A deterministic quadratic curve and analytical intersection renderer, with geometry and displayed values derived from the same equations.
A non-probabilistic uncertainty-envelope pattern that explicitly names the assumed K±0.10 range and retains OEM evidence as open.
Reusable unit-bearing specimen strips and a review-folio handoff with finite, pause-aware, reduced-motion-safe typography and line choreography.
limitations: All diagrams, units-as-labels, numerical values and relationships are illustrative; no actual plant inputs or equipment performance are represented.
K±0.10 is an authored illustrative assumption, not a measured tolerance, confidence interval or validated sensitivity range.
The four dimensional input symbols show provenance requirements but do not imply that diameter, length or roughness were populated or used in an actual hydraulic-loss calculation.
Calculation completion does not select equipment. Actual boundaries, input records, OEM evidence and human engineering review remain required.
Local module and SVG contract checks do not establish browser rendering or real-device visual acceptance.
